note_2026_08_17: Verify brief dispatched this same day named three 'unmined, not yet published, not already rejected' candidates for a deepen pass: Falso kapok (sheet 29/H501/RM/12), Ibrido di Quercia americana (sheet 30/H501/RM/12) and Melograno (sheet 73/H501/RM/12). All three are the San Sisto nursery cluster already in this file's blocked list (with sheet 28, the Cedar of Lebanon, as the fourth member) for the exact same reason: the Semenzaio comunale di San Sisto Vecchio is a working municipal nursery, generally closed to the public, open only on scheduled dates (FAI Giornate di Primavera, occasional 'domeniche ecologiche' such as 29 March). Reconfirmed by web search this pass (comune.roma.it NWS606658, 7colli.it, canaledieci.it 2025-08-30 all describe it as normally closed with periodic open days), nothing has changed. None of the three verify: they fail hard rule 10's first test (cannot enter without a scheduled/booked visit), the same as sheets 28 and 30 already recorded. The Melograno additionally fails the collectible-point test on its own register data (33 separate stems, no single trunk). No new trees delivered from this brief. Recorded here so a future brief-writer does not regenerate this exact same false-premise brief a third time.
note: Source pool is the 65 entries for comune di Roma in the MASAF national register, cross-read against the Lazio regional register (https://www.regione.lazio.it/sites/default/files/2025-11/Elenco-alberi-monumentali.xlsx, Nov 2025), which is the richer of the two: it carries the monumentality criteria per tree, a NOTE column, and a second sheet of trees REMOVED from the list with the reason. Six trees were published from this pass as rom_011 to rom_016, thickening the Villa Sciarra, Trastevere, Capitoline and Villa Borghese walks. Everything else is here. Do not quote 65 as a count of monumental trees in Rome: it is a count of register entries, six of them are 'insieme omogeneo' groups rather than single trees, and 22 of them stand inside a closed presidential estate. Rome's own municipal page NWS1195295 narrates only about 20 of them, the batch registered up to 2018; sheets numbered 57 and above have no municipal narrative at all, which is why several entries below are stuck at one source.

leads.name: Stone Pine of Villa Torlonia
leads.why_not_published: Second tallest tree on Rome's register and a textbook umbrella pine, but register-only: sheet 75 postdates the municipal narrative page. Note that a different Villa Torlonia stone pine, sheet 18, is on the Lazio REMOVED list as dead, so any pass shipping this one must be explicit about which is which. VITALITY RISK RAISED, 2026-08-08 (rom deepen verify pass): press coverage found this pass shows Villa Torlonia's whole tree stock under active safety felling. Il Messaggero/La Capitale (11 Dec 2025) report 19 trees felled after a stability survey rated them 'classe di cedimento D' (highest risk), including 4 Pinus pinea; RomaToday/La Capitale describe further urgent fellings continuing into 2026 (5 more trees in March 2026, though that batch was palms, an Aleppo pine and a Judas tree, not stone pines). None of the coverage found names which specific stone pines were among the 4 felled in December. The Lazio Nov 2025 xlsx (which is our source for this lead) still listed sheet 75 as active, i.e. before the December felling, so the register cannot settle this either way. Given the confirmed sibling already dead (sheet 18) and 4 more stone pines felled in the same park weeks after our register snapshot, this tree should NOT ship without a specific, dated confirmation that sheet 75 itself is still standing. Not blocked (not confirmed dead), but do not verify from the register alone; needs a targeted post-December-2025 check, ideally the Lazio register's next update or a dated photo/observation. CHECKED AGAIN 2026-08-26 (rom deepen verify pass): the risk picture has worsened rather than resolved. RomaToday (12 Jan 2026, 'Villa Torlonia, addio ad altri 9 alberi') reports a further felling round at the villa, and the same week a 120-year-old stone pine collapsed on Via dei Fori Imperiali, triggering a citywide re-inspection of Rome's stone pines with more fellings expected ('Dopo i pini crollati ai Fori Imperiali nuovi controlli sugli alberi. Ci saranno nuovi abbattimenti'). Still no source names sheet 75 specifically, in either direction. Given an active citywide stone-pine safety programme on top of Villa Torlonia's own repeated fellings, this tree is further than ever from a safe register-only ship; still needs a specific, dated sighting of this exact tree, not a park-wide vitality inference. CHECKED AGAIN 2026-09-11 (rom deepen verify pass): searched for the December 2025 felling list and any subsequent Villa Torlonia coverage naming Via Siracusa specifically; found only the same aggregate figures (19 trees felled, classe di cedimento D, 4 Pinus pinea among them, no locations given) already recorded above, nothing new. Confirmed sheet 75's locality (Via Siracusa, one of the villa's three real gate streets) and that it is a distinct sheet from the confirmed-dead sheet 18 (Viale Tiziano Terzani). Still no way to confirm this exact tree survived the felling programme; leaving as an unresolved lead rather than shipping on the register alone, per the standing note above.

Genuinely still register-only; do not fold it into rom_024 as a pair since only one of the two is independently corroborated, and folding would overstate what is known about this one.

leads.why_not_published: Third thickest trunk on the Roma register, but the Lazio register's own NOTE says it was burned in a fire in 2025 and asserts its monumental character is unaffected. That is the register's judgement of a tree that caught fire eight months ago, not a vitality check. Far south of the city besides. Needs eyes before it can ever ship. [SKIPPED 2026-08-14 by the write pass] Two reasons, either sufficient: it sits about 14 km south of the centre, beyond the 30-minute day-trip boundary that keeps a tree on a city page, and its vitality after the 2025 fire has still not been checked by anyone. Belongs to a southern Rome or Ostia page if one is ever made, and needs eyes first either way.

leads.name: Almonds of the Villa di Faonte
leads.why_not_published: Two registered almonds 90m apart at Via delle Vigne Nuove 280, an address attached to the so-called Villa di Faonte. Register-only, access unverified, and a monumental almond would be a genuine curiosity, so worth checking whether the grounds are public before writing it off. Real February blossom peak if it ever ships. CHECKED 2026-08-08 (rom deepen verify pass): RomaToday reports the Villa di Faonte archaeological park itself reopened to the public after ten years closed ('Villa di Faonte, dopo dieci anni apre il parco: restano sbarrati i casali'), access from Via delle Vigne Nuove and Via del Passo del Turchino, which is encouraging on general access but does not confirm the two specific almond trees are inside the reopened area rather than on an adjacent closed plot, and no second source names the trees themselves. Still needs a dedicated look, not part of this pass's briefed cluster. [SKIPPED 2026-08-14 by the write pass] Two separately registered almonds (sheets 58 and 59) 90 metres apart at the same address: no single obvious place to stand, so it fails the collectible-point test as one entry, and access to the specific plot the trees stand on is still unconfirmed. Either almond could ship alone once someone establishes it is inside the reopened archaeological park. RESOLVED 2026-09-11 (rom deepen verify pass): sheet 58, locally known as the Mandorlo di Nerone, now has a genuine second independent source, ilregistrodeglialberi.it (registration #14221, last field survey 2026-03-08, girth 350cm against the register's 360cm, health status Good), which settles both vitality and identity for that one tree. The park-reopening question is also settled: RomaToday and vivereroma.org both date the Parco di Villa di Faonte's public reopening to 26 April 2026, current as of this pass; turismoroma.it's 'currently not open to visitors' page is stale and describes the archaeological casali, not the open park where the almonds stand. Delivered as rom_031. Sheet 59 (girth 300cm, 41.954167/12.537167, about 110m from sheet 58) still has no second source of its own and stays here as an open lead; it could ship as a companion tree once one is found, but folding it into rom_031 as a pair would overstate what is known about it specifically.

leads.name: Sughera of Parco Francesco Salerno
leads.why_not_published: 2026-08-26 verify pass (rom deepen). Named as unresearched in this file's note_2026_08_14 and flagged there as 'the cheapest of the four' because it names a public park. It genuinely does: info.roma.it confirms Parco Francesco Salerno at Via della Riserva grande, Casalotti (Z.XLVIII), part of the far northwest green corridor near the Riserva Naturale dell'Insugherata, free and open. The blocker is distance and transit rather than access: the park sits 14 km northwest of the centre, well past Rome's other rejected trees on this measure, and current (2026) local reporting on Casalotti's isolation (RomaToday, on the Battistini-Casalotti Bus Rapid Transit project) describes 55 minutes to over an hour by bus to cover just 6 km to the nearest interchange, or 21 minutes on foot to reach Battistini metro station alone. That fails the roughly-30-minute day-trip boundary by a wide margin. Genuinely a fine free tree in a real reserve; belongs to a Casalotti or Insugherata page if one is ever made, not a Rome city page. STATUS SET 2026-08-30: beyond the roughly-30-minute day-trip boundary (14km / same far corridor), confirmed by this pass; not merely unresearched.

note_2026_08_26: Verify pass 2026-08-26 (rom deepen). Two findings for whoever briefs the next pass. First, passcheck.py --brief's 'unmined' register list (candidates within 80m of a live tree are flagged, everything else is called unmined) is STALE for the San Sisto nursery / Porta Capena cluster: it printed the Cedro del Libano (sheet 28, 500cm), Falso kapok (sheet 29), Ibrido di Quercia americana (sheet 30) and Platano comune (sheet 06, Parco di Porta Capena) as unmined candidates, and all four are already in this file's blocked list (access-restricted nursery; homogeneous plane stand). This is the same false premise note_2026_08_17 already recorded for three of the four; passcheck's proximity check does not cross-reference data/leads/*.json's blocked list, only published trees, so this will keep recurring until that script is fixed. Second, of the four sheet 61/64/78/81 candidates named in note_2026_08_14: sheet 61 (Eucalyptus of Forte Ardeatino) verified and shipped as rom_030 (data/research/rome-verified.json). Sheets 64, 78 and 81 are now recorded above as leads: all three sit in far-out corridors (Casalotti/Insugherata northwest, or the deep-south Ostia corridor) that likely fail the roughly-30-minute day-trip boundary; sheet 81 was checked directly and confirmed to fail it, 64 and 78 are flagged by proximity to confirmed-far trees rather than individually checked.
